heuristics: Class walk behaves as a random function on N'=(r-1)/6 classes up to a 3% length margin (Teske 2001, table size 2^16).
Distinguished-point bits and table-index bits of the canonical x-coordinate are independent and uniform.

Fruitless cycles start with probability at most 4/2^16 per step (derived 2-cycle rate 1/(6*2^16); cycles of length L at most Bell(L)*2^(-16*ceil(L/2))); they are detected at a fixed period of 64 steps, walked once, and escaped by doubling the cycle's smallest class, at a charge of 300 units per event.
limitations: Costs use the fixed reference prices C=2000 and 383 instructions per Fp multiplication; per-step instruction counts are itemised estimates with a reserve.
Memory of about 2^36 bytes is needed for the distinguished-point store; memory carries no score.
Not a novel attack: textbook parallel collision search with automorphisms.
